chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun al-Fami (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said:
Be good to your parents, and your children will be good to you. Be chaste regarding the women of others, and your women will be chaste.

key_terms.بروا: Birr - to be righteous/good toward, especially parents (filial piety)
key_terms.عفوا: Iffah/Iffu - to be chaste, to abstain from what is unlawful
key_terms.نساء الناس: The women of the people, i.e., women who are not lawful to you

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about being good to parents and chastity?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches a profound ethical principle of reciprocity: filial piety towards parents is rewarded with devoted children, and maintaining chastity towards the women of others ensures the chastity of one's own womenfolk. This teaching was delivered to his companion Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, and it reflects the Islamic emphasis on the interconnectedness of moral conduct and its consequences within family and society.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Harun al-Fami (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. `Abd al-Jabbar from `Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Najran from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Rabat from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:
Be good to your parents, and your children will be good to you. Be chaste with the women of the people, and your women will be chaste.
